notes: Read SKILL.md (591 lines) and references/openapi-codegen.md, openapi-security.md, openapi-setup.md, openapi-testing.md, openapi-tools.md, openapi-versioning-strategies.md in full. Spec-first OpenAPI 3.x workflow: info/servers, paths, $ref components, error schemas, security schemes, Spectral/swagger-cli validation, openapi-generator codegen, versioning and breaking-change detection, plus example tests and CI steps.

Medium because the workflow tells the agent to run npm tooling: SKILL.md:271-297 runs npx @stoplight/spectral-cli, swagger-cli, openapi-diff and @openapitools/openapi-generator-cli (which writes generated code to ./generated/), and openapi-setup.md:124/138/144 and openapi-codegen.md:9 use 'npm install -g'. These are well-known packages from the official npm registry (not curl|sh), but versions are unpinned except openapitools.json's generator version 7.10.0; the agent should confirm global installs and codegen output paths with the user. No credentials are used and no live services are contacted beyond localhost dev servers.

Security guidance is sound: global bearer auth, HTTPS-only servers, CORS echoing an allowlisted origin, input constraints. Minor inaccuracies: openapi-versioning-strategies.md lists 'Adding new enum value' as non-breaking (can break strict clients); openapi-security.md defines a header parameter named 'RateLimit-*' (not valid OpenAPI); the .spectral.yaml custom rule in openapi-tools.md repeats keys under one rule (invalid YAML); swagger-cli is deprecated upstream. SKILL.md:469-592 is generic boilerplate (observer pattern, deployment checklist, STRIDE) unrelated to OpenAPI. The handoff names a 'contract-testing' skill that is optional and not bundled.
